name: Rowan Green Data LLC

profile.campus: Rowan Percheron Data Center Campus (Morrow County, OR)
profile.reading: This record is one of four tightly clustered OSM buildings this registry maps as "Percheron DC," on Tower Road in Morrow County, Oregon, approximately nine miles south of Interstate 84. Morrow County's own Planning Commission records confirm a real, government-processed land use case for this site: case numbers AC-145-23 (Comprehensive Plan amendment), ACM-146-23, and AZM-147-23 (zone map amendment), filed by applicant Rowan Percheron, LLC, seeking to rezone approximately 274 acres from Exclusive Farm Use (EFU) to General Industrial (MG) with a Limited Use Overlay Zone restricting development to data center operations only, evaluated under Morrow County Zoning Ordinance Article 8 and Oregon Administrative Rules 660-004-0010, including exceptions to Statewide Planning Goals 3 (Farmland), 11 (Public Facilities), and 14 (Urbanization). The case record, adopted by the Planning Commission, references a land use application, soils/geotechnical/wetland delineation reports, a traffic impact analysis and economic analysis summary, endangered-species and cultural-resource assessments, a water supply memorandum of understanding with the Port of Morrow, and correspondence with the Navy and area tribes, indicating a substantial, real industrial-scale project rather than a speculative or nominal filing. Morrow County has become one of Oregon's most significant data center corridors in recent years, anchored by a large Amazon build-out reported in 2022 at roughly $12 billion across at least five facilities, and the water-supply coordination with the Port of Morrow reflects the same regional water-availability questions that have drawn scrutiny to other large data center projects in the county. No building-specific square footage, MW capacity, or year-opened figure for this particular building was located in county planning materials or any operator website reachable this session; Rowan Green Data LLC and Rowan Percheron, LLC appear, per the county's own case record, to be closely related entities behind the same Tower Road project, though this registry has not independently confirmed the precise legal relationship between the two names.

That release focused on the Temple, Texas campus and did not mention the Morrow County, Oregon site this registry's facility rows are tagged to; Oregon operations not independently confirmed against a primary Rowan or Quinbrook source this session, only via trade press (Data Center Dynamics) and a local chamber-of-commerce business listing.
profile.oregon_project: Trade press (Data Center Dynamics) separately reports Rowan planning a 1 million sq ft data center campus in Morrow County, Oregon; local business registration confirms Rowan Green Data LLC DBA Rowan Digital Infrastructure as a Boardman, Oregon area chamber of commerce member
profile.flagship_campus: 800 MW multi-tenant campus in Temple, Texas, first phase 220 MW, nearing construction completion as of a January 2023 announcement

reading:
Rowan Green Data LLC, trading as Rowan Digital Infrastructure, was established in November 2020, originally as a joint venture between Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners and Birch Infrastructure and now a wholly owned Quinbrook portfolio company based in San Francisco. Its business is supplying powered land and infrastructure to data centre operators rather than always operating compute itself, which matters for how its rows in this registry should be read.

The four Oregon rows recorded here are not four data centres. They are four OpenStreetMap ways created in a single changeset on 21 April 2026 by one contributor, each named Percheron DC and each tagged with a proposed industrial building tag rather than a building tag. They are four proposed building footprints on one campus, traced from a site plan rather than surveyed, and as of their only version none is mapped as a constructed structure. A further sign that the tags were transcribed rather than observed is the owner field, which reads Rowan Digital Infrastructure Pty Ltd. That is an Australian company form and does not match the United States limited liability company named in the operator field.

The project itself is real and documented by its developer. Rowan's Percheron Data Center site places the campus roughly 11 miles southwest of Boardman in Morrow County, Oregon, on land owned for several years by Threemile Canyon Farms and never put to use because the soils are unproductive, bordering property owned by Portland General Electric and by the United States Navy. The coordinates stored in this registry, near 45.71 north and 119.82 west, are consistent with that description. Rowan states that no new transmission lines are required, that water would be supplied through the Port of Morrow delivery system, and that water use is expected to be minimal compared with other utility scale industrial projects that are not data centres.

The land use chronology, as the developer describes it, runs from third party studies in the winter of 2022, to a rezoning application in the spring of 2023, a Morrow County Planning Commission recommendation on 25 July 2023, county approval on 25 September 2023, and site plan approvals in late 2023 and early 2024. Employment is described only as dozens of full time jobs with several hundred indirect and induced positions, at wages the developer says are well above the county median household income.

What is absent is more striking than what is present. Rowan publishes no megawatt figure of any kind for Percheron, no acreage, no building count, no square footage and no named tenant. Its description of the site as net zero and powered entirely by renewable energy is a statement about procurement, not a capacity figure, and should not be read as one. Quinbrook's flagship Rowan campus, an 800 MW multi tenant project at Temple, Texas with a 220 MW first phase, is a separate site and is not represented in this registry.
